note: How content moves and renders: the address grammar a reference shares across the repo, the delivery modes pages/toss-render.html accepts, and the toss routes that map a content type to the page that renders it. Read by show-repo's Map view (Transport tab). The `routes` block is the owner of toss-render.html's TOSS_ROUTES literal, which stays inlined so the critical render path takes no fetch; tools/test/routes-manifest.test.mjs holds the two in step.
precedence: Every parameter below is read fragment first, query as fallback: toss-render for its own params, and the renderer pages through lib/url-params.js. Put a payload in the fragment, which never reaches a server and so escapes the roughly 8KB cap the Pages edge enforces with a 414 (PR #165). An address is short, so either form works, and a routed toss delivers ?src= through toss-render's params shim rather than over the wire.

grammar.role: One way to name a file in any repo, at any ref. The ':' before the path is unambiguous because git forbids ':' in ref names; no @ref means the repo's default branch.

usedBy.where: a repo's pages catalog and stage.files

modes.note: The page rides in the fragment, so nothing is hosted and nothing reaches a server. Absolute-URL CDN dependencies work; same-repo relative ones do not.
The uncompressed sibling of #gz=. Same sandbox, longer URL.
Points the frame at a URL rather than carrying the bytes. A site sending X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors will refuse to load.

Fetched live through the contents API, so private repos and un-deployed branches render. Same-origin means the frame could read this origin's stored token, which is why the allowlist refuses any other owner outright. The browser-local token means a fresh or in-app browser may 404; fall back to #gz= or a published artifact.

A typed toss: the key names a renderer from the routes below, the value addresses the content. Resolves onto address mode, so the caller addresses the CONTENT and toss-render stays a schema-blind router that never parses the envelope.

The renderer side of the split, not a toss-render param. A routed toss resolves into this: toss-render renders the renderer page and the params shim delivers ?src= to the page's own read. Reaching a renderer directly with ?src= works the same; the route is shorthand, not a gate. Renderer pages read it fragment first like everything else, so #src= is accepted too.

routes.renders: A chat or trawl results envelope: search hits across conversations, annotated and rendered together.

Data as something readable rather than a raw blob: a CSV, a JSON array, a log, in a multi-mode viewer (table, tree, preview, code, raw). Bare bytes need no wrapper; an items envelope adds several files with a default view each.
